what: A bundle of long lines converging on a vanishing point at screen center (WebGL, three) — the lines are strips parallel to the camera axis so perspective makes them radiate, and sound lines (channels) swell sideways by the coarse waveform amplitude into accent-colored waves — only three randomly chosen lines surge boldly, the other channels are small ripples. Waves flow along the lines (2 to 4 speed per line), fade at the front and back ends, a bright node passes along each strip once every 20s, and the grain texture sparkles. 22 thin gray lines and 260 dust points drift forward, with a faint ring at the center. The camera turns slowly at .03rad per second and tilts toward the mouse up to .06rad. Turning a channel on (fx:channel) makes its wave 1.6x wider and brighter within .4s

options.thin: Number of thin gray lines, default 22
options.speed: Waveform and dust flow multiplier, default 1
options.tilt: Tilt toward the mouse (rad), default .06 — 0 means it doesn’t follow the mouse
options.on: Channel numbers to turn on at the start (comma-separated), default none
options.fx:channel: Send to the element to toggle the channel on and off — new CustomEvent("fx:channel", { detail: { index: 2, on: true } })
options.loud: Number of channels that surge boldly, default 3 — other channels only ripple (.2–.45), 1.6x when on

note: If three is missing, the motion part loads library/_vendor/three@0.168.0/build/three.cjs itself and moves it onto window.THREE (it is a CJS build, so window.exports is opened briefly). If the caller preloads it, it attaches right away. Colors --kf-accent · --kf-ink · --kf-ink-soft are read when attaching

from.where: index.html .us-visual__stage — measured the original js/visualizer.js (sound mixer hero) and rewrote it with our shader
